Definition: from G3844 and G2955; to bend beside, i.e. lean over (so as to peer within):--look (into), stoop down.
BiblicalUsage: Parakyptō means to stoop down, to bend over and look in. Mary stands without at the sepulchre weeping, and as she weeps she stoops down and looks into the sepulchre; and James says the man who looks into the perfect law of liberty and continues therein shall be blessed in his deed.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that stooping is the posture of faith: Mary bends to look into an empty tomb, and the doer bends to look into the law of liberty, and both find more than they expected.
